newsitem.title: CHINA: China to set up large chain store groups.
newsitem.headline: China to set up large chain store groups.

text.p: China is to set up several large scale chain store groups in the next five to 10 years in a bid to make its domestic retail sector more competitive, the People's Daily said on Tuesday.
The Ministry of Domestic Trade planned to create several chain store groups with annual sales of more than 10.0 billion yuan ($1.2 billion), the newspaper said in its overseas edition.
It did not say specifically how it would encourage the creation of the store groups or which groups would be assisted.
The ministry this year hoped to promote three chain stores with sales over one billion yuan, more than 50 with sales over 100 million yuan, and more than 30 with over 50 outlets, it said.
By the end of 1996 China had more than 700 chain stores with a total of more than 10,000 outlets, the newspaper said.
However, most of the chain stores were too small, averaging 14 outlets each, and only five percent had sales over 100 million yuan, it said.
China has been trying to set up larger and more efficient companies in many different sectors in a bid to make domestic enterprises more competitive on the local and international markets.
